reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch Re-Harden (mat_g1_mg_q1_2), 2026-08-19

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The samples directly fulfill the MATATAG learning competency to compose and decompose triangles, squares, and rectangles. Shape composition is tested in items such as "Two identical squares are placed side by side. What shape do they form?" and "Two triangles are placed together, matching their longest straight edges. What shape do they form?". Shape decomposition is assessed in items like "A long rectangle is cut across its width into two equal squares. What two shapes are made?" and "A square is cut on a slant, from one corner to the opposite corner. What two shapes are made?".

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The items comprehensively cover the three target geometric figures (triangles, squares, and rectangles) across both composition and decomposition operations. Composition covers pairing squares to form a rectangle, pairing triangles along their longest edges to form a rectangle ("Two identical triangles are rotated to fit together into a rectangle. What shape is made?") or a square ("Two identical triangles are joined along their matching straight edges to make a 4-sided shape with equal sides. What shape is formed?"). Decomposition covers cutting a rectangle into squares ("A long rectangle is cut across its width into two equal squares. What two shapes are made?"), cutting a rectangle into rectangles ("A rectangle is cut into two equal pieces down the middle. What two shapes are made?"), and cutting a square into triangles ("A square is cut on a slant, from one corner to the opposite corner. What two shapes are made?").

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The language and cognitive load are perfectly tuned for Grade 1 Quarter 1 learners. Spatial manipulation is described using clear, tangible visual actions such as "cut across its width into two equal squares", "placed side by side", and "cut on a slant, from one corner to the opposite corner". The questions avoid extraneous developmental jargon while preserving geometric precision appropriate for beginning primary students.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The sample set demonstrates excellent variation in geometric transformations and cutting orientations. It tests horizontal/vertical cuts ("A rectangle is cut into two equal pieces down the middle. What two shapes are made?"), transverse cuts ("A long rectangle is cut across its width into two equal squares. What two shapes are made?"), diagonal cuts ("A square is cut on a slant, from one corner to the opposite corner. What two shapes are made?"), side-by-side adjacency ("Two identical squares are placed side by side. What shape do they form?"), and rotational edge alignment ("Two identical triangles are rotated to fit together into a rectangle. What shape is made?").

competency_alignment.rationale: The questions align strictly with the target competency. Every item focuses solely on composing and decomposing 2D plane figures (triangles, squares, rectangles) without introducing out-of-scope concepts such as perimeter, area calculations, formal angle measures, 3D solids, or coordinate systems.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The questions are qualitatively framed around 2D shape identification and spatial composition/decomposition without requiring numerical measurements or complex dimensional scaling, making them entirely appropriate for Grade 1 Quarter 1.
